title: Place Value, Comparing and Ordering Numbers
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Place Value, Comparing and Ordering Numbers. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Place value

In base ten, each position is ten times the position to its right. In (\(6,704.308\)), the 7 represents (\(7,000\)), the 3 represents (\(3/10\)), and the 8 represents (\(8/1,000\)). Expanded form is (\(6,704.308=6,000+700+4+0.3+0.008\)). Zero can hold a place even when it contributes no value.

Compare and order

On a number line, values increase from left to right. For negative values, the one closer to zero is greater: (\(-3>-8\)). To compare decimals, align decimal points and append trailing zeroes if useful; (\(0.600>0.598\)). Leading zeroes do not change magnitude, and trailing zeroes after a decimal do not change value.

Rounding and significant figures

To round to a place, inspect the digit immediately to its right: 0–4 leaves the retained digit unchanged; 5–9 increases it by one. Significant figures begin at the first nonzero digit. In (\(0.004786\)), the first two significant figures are 4 and 7, so the value to two significant figures is (\(0.0048\)). Rounding to unit u gives an error no greater than half a unit, subject to the tie convention.

Worked example: To the nearest hundred, (\(18,749\)) becomes (\(18,700\)), since the tens digit is 4. To two significant figures it becomes (\(19,000\)), since the third significant digit is 7.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Pad the shorter decimal on the right; never compare decimal digit counts alone.
  • For negative values, compare magnitudes and reverse the order.
  • Mark the requested place, then inspect exactly one digit to its right.
  • Use scientific notation to compare very large or small values.
  • State the requested precision; “round 2,347” is incomplete without a place or significant-figure count.

Common errors

  • Appending zeroes to a whole number changes its value; appending decimal zeroes does not.
  • Rounding an intermediate value repeatedly can accumulate error.
  • At an exact halfway value, follow the rounding convention specified by the question.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Place values: (\(...,10^3,10^2,10^1,10^0,10^{-1},10^{-2},...\)).
  • Nearest unit u: absolute rounding error is at most (\(u/2\)).
  • Significant figures start at the first nonzero digit.
  • Check that the rounded value is close to the original and has the requested precision.
  • Keep extra digits during intermediate calculations and round at the end.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    Which is greater: (\(0.505\)) or (\(0.55\))?

    1. (\(0.505\))
    2. (\(0.55\))
    3. They are equal
    4. Cannot be compared
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(0.55\))

    Write (\(0.55\)) as (\(0.550\)). Since (\(550\)) thousandths is greater than (\(505\)) thousandths, (\(0.55>0.505\)).

  2. Core:

    What is the place value of 7 in (\(6,704.3\))?

    1. (\(7\))
    2. (\(70\))
    3. (\(700\))
    4. (\(7,000\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(7,000\))

    The 7 is in the thousands place, so its place value is (\(7\times1,000=7,000\)).

  3. Foundation:

    What is the value of the digit 6 in (\(48,623.5\))?

    1. (\(6\))
    2. (\(60\))
    3. (\(600\))
    4. (\(6,000\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(600\))

    The 6 is in the hundreds place, so its value is (\(600\)).

  4. Standard:

    Round (\(0.004786\)) to two significant figures.

    1. (\(0.0047\))
    2. (\(0.0048\))
    3. (\(0.00479\))
    4. (\(0.0050\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(0.0048\))

    The first two significant digits are 4 and 7; the next digit is 8, so round 7 up: (\(0.0048\)).

  5. Challenge:

    Which interval contains the positive values that round to (\(3.7\)) to the nearest tenth under the usual half-up rule?

    1. (\([3.65,3.75\)))
    2. (\([3.7,3.8\)))
    3. (\((3.65,3.75])
    4. ([3.6,3.8)\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\([3.65,3.75\)))

    The midpoint boundaries are 3.65 and 3.75. The lower tie rounds up to 3.7, while 3.75 rounds to 3.8; therefore the interval is (\([3.65,3.75\))).
